newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - Sept 6.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - Sept 6.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

The Development Allowance Authority is set to warn companies applying for the infrastructure bond tax concession not to proceed unless they meet strict guidelines in an effort to reduce possible widespread abuse of the tax concession which could cost the Federal Government revenue losses of up to A$7 billion over the next 15 years. Page 1.

Although he said "at face value" there was "little need for monetary policy action", Reserve Bank governor Bernie Fraser suggested in Tokyo yesterday that unemployment remained a major concern for policy makers and that, provided inflation and wages were kept in check, interest rates could be further reduced to ease joblessness. Page 3.

In response to Taiwanese President Lee Teng-hui's comment on his wish to visit Australia, Primary Industries Minister John Anderson said in Taipei yesterday that "such high-level visits are precluded" by the one-China policy. However, despite protests from Beijing, Anderson also confirmed Australia's willingness to sell uranium to Taiwan. Page 3.

In the first definite step by a major Australian bank into Internet banking, National Australia Bank has formed a joint venture with IBM and at least 15 foreign banks to offer electronic commerce, home and Internet banking. NAB's move into the INET jointventure is an attempt to head-off attempts by non-bank competitors such as Microsoft, GE Capital and Telstra to offer banking services as part of an existing customer relationship. Page 5.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Employers have condemned the ACTU's framework to achieve higher living standards for all workers, approved on the final day of a three-day ACTU Council meeting at the Victorian town of Lorne. According to employers, the ACTU's decision to set a wage target for enterprise bargaining as high as 15 per cent above award rates is in conflict with the notion of enterprise bargaining. Page 1.

Although he told a Tokyo seminar that Australia could look forward to another year of reasonable economic growth and low inflation, Reserve Bank governor Bernie Fraser said he saw little reason to make a second interest rate cut as the "encouraging inflation outlook" had already been taken into account when the bank pushed official rates down on July 31. Page 1.

After declaring the Federal Government's redesign of labour market assistance would have a higher success rate than the former Government's Working Nation, Employment Minister Amanda Vanstone conceded yesterday that the reforms could see a rise in long-tem unemployment and the Government might need to provide additional referral support services for the long-term unemployed who are ruled ineligible for labour market assistance. Page 1.

Almost 125,000 students will be ineligible for Austudy or have their payments reduced in 1997 following the Government's decision to toughen the Austudy Actual Means Test and raise the age at which students qualify for Austudy at the independent rate from 22 to 25, in an effort to save A$460 million in the next four years. Page 3.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

In response to building anger over the threat of reduced services and heavy job losses, the New South Wales Government announced yesterday that it no longer needed to slash funding to hospitals in Sydney's north and east and would fund new health services by cutting running costs across all departments. Page 1.

Although New South Wales Community Services Minister Ron Dyer claims he has long been dissatisfied with Department head Des Semple's performance, the State Opposition says Dyer's decision to sack the public servant is a vindictive attempt to silence a critic. Semple complained to the Independent Commission Against Corruption earlier this year about an attempt by the Public Employment Office to remove him and downgrade his position as director-general of the Community Services Department. Page 1.

Plans for the Homebush Bay Olympic site, prepared by a design team led by the New South Wales Government architect Chris Johnson, reveal Homebush will be transformed into a bustling township with tree-lined avenues, 60-metre-wide boulevards, European-style piazzas and major pieces of art and sculpture. The streets will echo Homebush Bay's grid of old paddocks, fences and stock routes, becoming the "urban heart" of Sydney's Olympic village. Page 2.

In an effort to cut A$2.1 million from its annual budget, ABC Radio will reduce staff by 30, downgrade local news bulletins and slash travel costs. At least 22 of the 30 jobs will be in news, including nine fewer reporters in New South Wales and programs Radio National AM and Saturday AM will be axed. Page 3.
THE AGE

The Anti-Discrimination Tribunal yesterday approved the development of a recreation and health centre for men, in particular gay men, proposed by Soreni Holdings, which has been operating gay venues for 20 years. The St Kilda complex will include a gymnaium, massage rooms, a sauna, a cafe, a beauty salon and conference rooms. Page A1.

Growing tension and disagreement between managers have stalled a final decision on what programs will be cut from the Australian Broadcasting Corporation line-up to meet a A$2.1 million budget cut. AM, PM, The World Today, early and late news bulletins, nternational cricket and rugby league are all being considered for the axe. Page A1.

The Melbourne Coroners Court heard yesterday that the ambulance Intergraph dispatch system suffered backlogs on busy days because there were only two dispatch terminals through which all emergency calls were funnelled and the system crashed for 14 hours on the same day Keith Cheong died of a heart attack after a mobile intensive care ambulance took nearly 30 minutes to arrive. Page A3.

The Australian Chamber of Manufactures' Allan Handberg warned yesterday that the Federal Government's budget cuts in industry assistance, particularly the decision to slash the research and development tax concession, could deter future investment in Victoria, hampering the efforts of the State Government to court investment. Page A3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
